method: One procedure, fitted on the public training pages only. (1) A glyph chain over the whole line, with the word space and the line end as ordinary symbols; each glyph is drawn given the four symbols before it, or, 6 times in 10, given only the two before it. It starts afresh at each line, from one start mark for a line that opens a paragraph and another for any other line. (2) The table drifts: the writer plans a book of 780 lines (15% of the manuscript's lines, the size of a sample of pages) and at each point uses counts from a window of 20 consecutive public pages that slides from the first page to the last as the book goes on (40 steps; the whole-text table is mixed in at weight 0.1). Paragraph-opening lines follow the same schedule at their own pace (their share of lines on the public pages, 14%). Lines written after the planned end use the last window. (3) Two kinds of reuse at the start of any word but the first of a line. With probability 0.25 the writer takes one of the last 15 words written (on a paragraph-opening line, only words already on that line) and changes one glyph of it to another that the chain allows between its neighbours. With probability 0.25 (ordinary lines only) it writes again, whole, a familiar word: one that stands at least twice among the last 300 words written. In both cases it prefers a word whose first glyph the chain allows after what was just written. No rule names a glyph, a word, a position in the line other than its start, a section or a Currier language. Lines holding a four-word run of the manuscript are redrawn. 'lines' are ordinary lines, 'first_lines' paragraph-opening lines. How it got here, each step forced by a fact on the record: the paragraph mark by F-008; the drift at the pace of the book by F-009 and F-011; the two-sided glyph change by F-013 (one-sided changes give 2.16 bits); short-context draws and whole copies of familiar words only by F-014 with the level of within-page reuse (whole copies of any recent word cost singletons, 0.58 to 0.65; almost none cost reuse, 0.21 to 0.24); whole copies from a long memory, not from the last line, by the bound on repetition from the line above (copies of the last 15 words overshoot it, 0.029 to 0.046); no reuse in a line's first word by F-006 (reuse there shortens line-opening words, 4.39 to 4.58 against 4.83). All settings were chosen on the public practice split. Local check for F-019, practice split: 6.31 on this text (seed 1; manuscript 8.46, threshold 3), passing the within-page shuffle; five further runs pass too (seeds 2 to 4: 5.34, 5.79, 4.96; fitted on every other public page only, both halves: 7.03, 4.31). Nothing in the procedure names p or f: a paragraph-opening line is written by the same chain from its own opening mark, and the gallows spread along the line through the chain's context of four symbols and through reuse confined to that line. For comparison the plain chain with the same opening mark but no such reuse (the text of R-011) gives 1.47 and fails, so the fact does separate procedures that treat the whole first line apart from those that only mark its first word; it does not need language. The text is the same seed-1 text sent against F-011 to F-018; it was generated before this fact was written and was not tuned to it. Sampling: the table drifts over a planned book of 780 lines, the size of the sample of pages, so the text stands for a sample of a whole book and not for a contiguous stretch (this fact does not depend on distance between pages in any case).
